g11-history-uh7-t1.overview: The Christian Kingdom under the Restored Solomonic Dynasty sits inside States, Principalities, Population Movements and Interactions in Ethiopia. Population movements run through Unit 7 of Grade 11 History, aligned to the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the Christian kingdom under the restored Solomonic dynasty and its feudal Gult system. Then the expansion of Islam and the Muslim sultanates along the Zeyla trade routes. Next, the western, southern, and central states with their indigenous religions. Also the long wars between the Christian highland kingdom and the sultanate of Adal under Imam Ahmad. Finally, the population movements of the Somali, Afar, Argoba, and Oromo peoples. Students will also learn how these population movements shaped the peoples of Ethiopia today.
objectives: Explain how the Solomonic dynasty consolidated its power.
Describe the Muslim sultanates and the Zeyla trade.
Analyse the causes of the war between the Christian kingdom and Adal.
Trace the population movements of the Oromo and their neighbours.
Discuss the Gadaa system and the Moggassa institution.
g11-history-uh7-t1.simple:
The Christian Kingdom under the Restored Solomonic Dynasty in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, Yikuno Amlak, the Solomonic legend, and the Kibre Negest.
  • Then the Gult land system, the roving capitals, and the Zeyla trade.

The Christian Kingdom under the Restored Solomonic Dynasty — the essentials. First, Yikuno Amlak, the Solomonic legend, and the Kibre Negest. Then the Gult land system, the roving capitals, and the Zeyla trade.
